name: A Future Task
objectiveText: Speak with High Explorer Magellas in Ironforge .

comments.body: It's funny coming back to this quest reading the comments and knowing that we had to wait until Cataclysm to come out just to get through the gates.
replies: Think of the new players who've never played the expansions! They have so much story to look forward to! It's like when you watch an old TV show for the first time as your friends nod knowingly at the mysteries to be revealed in the next season.

comments.body:
Ok, here is what i was thinking. Not sure if it has been said elsewhere, but will post it anyways. The Stone Watcher talks about the Creators wanting to revisit Azeroth. They also state that the Plates of Uldum have been distributed to those that deserve them, or something to that effect. 

**Spoilers**

From the spirit in Uldaman we know that the Creator's made a matrix and created two races. The Troggs, and the Dwarves. What if leaders of these two races, or maybe not leaders but spiritual/historicaly ancestral characters were given the Plates of Uldum to hold until the Creators return. To me it seems that the Troggs work for the Creators, and the Dwarves work agianst the Creators. What if the Troggs were holding the plates, waiting for the Creators to return to open back up Uldum? Maybe the Giants as well, as they were placed at Uldum as guardians? 
Anyone know wof any boss encounters with Giants or Troggs around lvl 48+? Just some thoughts

We know for sure Blizzard is not intending to make an instance for each element (earth, water, air, fire) or at least not make them one after the other.

[ul]
  [li][b]Molten Core[/b] - Ragnaros (God of Fire)
[/li]
  [li][b]Blackwing Lair[/b] - Nefarian (no god but big brother of Onyxia, another part of WoW lore different from the gods of elements)
[/li]
  [li][b]Onyxia[/b] - epic vendor (i personally don't know what the lore is about her)
[/li]
  [li][b]Ahn'Qiraj[/b] - defenitly not linked to Thunderaan (God of Air) but connected to the great war between the Brood of Nozdoromu and the God of ?bugs? C'Tun (who on a sidenote seemed to me from the lore to act like Pinky and the Brain, planning to take over the world :P)
[/li]
  [li][b]Naxxramas[/b] - Kel'Thuzad, Lich King (totally not connected to Uldaman, Uldam and Uldea)
[/li]
[/ul]

So if i'm not mistaken from what we have ingame at this time there is no promise of when they will make the continuation available for us. So, do not ask or search for continuation for this quest as it seems it's a high lvl instance to come in the far future.
Then again ... i might be wrong ;)
replies: In Day of the Dragon, Neltharian stole a batch of Red dragon eggs, though he failed to get all of them, at least one cart-full was stolen. The other carts can be found in ruins of the battle in the Wetlands. Of that brood, he took a consort, and using his magic, transformed them into pseudo-black dragons. He hid some of the eggs on Draenor, which later hatched as the ill-fated Nether Drakes. His consort gave him two eggs who were actually his children before some unknown fate befell her; Onyxia and Nefarian. At some point after these events, Deathwing vanished, possibly captured by Alexstrazsa

comments.body:
One theory I've had about Warcraft Lore is that it tries to play on double entandres (sp?) and multiple meanings. 

Much of Warcraft history reflects the developement process of the Warcraft series.

Thus, one idea I have come up with is that the Titans who are supposed to "not come back" makes it so that we will not have to encounter them as bosses. Though the guardian at Uldum states that the "Creators" will come back. Possibly a reference to the Game Devs, maybe a little credit to them for their Hard work. The guardian even comments on their constant reshaping of the bioshpere that is Azeroth. Just as we see with each new content update how Azeroth is reshaped and rebuilt.

The "One's who are Worthy" could refer to GMs or the Map Terrain Testers and Game Engine Testers. Thus Uldum itself being the physical representation of a "Test Zone" within the game. 

Therefore I believe that Uldum is a homage to the Developers who created this great game.
Does anyone know what happons after, or where you go to continue the quest? I want to see Uldum.

Great Quest string, keeps you on the edge of your seat, Yes, kind of a letdown, but it's my beliefe that after BC (Burning Crusade) release, there will be an ULDUM instance. I think they are going to be doing a lot of retrofitting to Tanaris in general, and what more than having a whopping 3 instances in one zone. Zul'farrak, Caverns of Time, and Uldum. I feel that later, this string will continue to a Raid encounter, which I am hoping has to do with the makers in Uldum. Again, i could be wrong, but this is my hope as of now.

-Wenduki-
60 Rogue
9/25/06

This is indeed a bit of a let down, but we do learn some important things: Blizzard plans to reintroduce the Titans in a glorious return to Azeroth, but the world will be going downhill before that time, like, say, the invasion of the Burning Legion, since they only revisit a world when things have gone fubar.  Uldum, as it turns out, is the lab from which they worked on renovating the planet, like the creation of the Earthen and the sea giants.  As for the discs, the Titans have a set (or sets), and they can make more if needed.  Otherwise, the Stone Watcher could have meant that for the time being, only the Titans have the keys, and that's the way they meant for it to be.  Until they return, there's no way to get inside Uldum.
I can only assume it will be opened in a future patch
